title: Closest to the Sun in winter

probes.question: What causes the seasons?
options: Changes in Earth's distance from the Sun

probes.question: True or false: Earth is closest to the Sun during the Northern Hemisphere's winter.

image.alt: The whole Earth seen from Apollo 17, showing Africa, Madagascar, swirling clouds and Antarctica against black space.
image.credit: NASA/Apollo 17 crew; taken by either Harrison Schmitt or Ron Evans / Wikimedia Commons

body.question: In which month is Earth closest to the Sun?
body.reveal: Earth is closest to the Sun in early January and farthest in early July, so distance works against the Northern Hemisphere's seasons. The real cause is Earth's tilt, about 23.4 degrees, which changes how high the Sun climbs in the sky.
